questions.prompt: Why could some historical stories not qualify under the previous rules?
options: The connected buildings had changed too much or disappeared.
The public had to nominate groups rather than individuals.
The national scheme accepted workplaces but excluded homes.
The people involved had to have lived in London.
questions.explanationZh: 此前要求建筑仍在且可辨认，因此拆除或变化过大成为障碍。

questions.prompt: What condition applies to a group being honoured?
options: It must still be working in its original building.
It must have received a community grant this year.
It must have started twenty years ago or earlier and stopped operating.
It must have worked in both Plymouth and Liverpool.
questions.explanationZh: s10同时给出成立至少二十年和不再运作两个条件。

questions.prompt: How are the two schemes organised?
options: English Heritage runs both, with local councils choosing sites.
Historic England runs the national one; English Heritage runs London’s.
Community groups run the national one; Historic England runs London’s.
The culture department runs London’s; English Heritage runs the national one.
questions.explanationZh: s11明确区分两个机构及其对应计划。

questions.prompt: What does the rule change mean for a redeveloped site?
options: It will receive a plaque before the application deadline.
It can qualify without a connection to a historical person.
It receives priority over buildings that still look the same.
It is no longer excluded solely because its building was replaced.
questions.explanationZh: 建筑被替代不再单独导致排除，但贡献、地点联系等其他条件仍存在，也不保证获牌或优先。
